clue.text: Writer of book with purpose entertaining everyone

indicators.note: to entertain guests is to have them inside your home, so one word holds the others

parts.note: B is the standard abbreviation for book
everyone means all of them
the point of something is its purpose

explanation.surface: An author with a mission whose book keeps the whole world amused.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Writer' suggests an author, but it is the pen itself; the purpose word holds the others.
explanation.definitionFit: A ballpoint is a pen, and a pen is an implement for writing.

clue.text: Cry over lover about to leave dance

indicators.note: turned over means read upside down, so the word runs backwards in a down entry

parts.note: to sob is to cry

indicators.note: whatever is told to leave departs, so those letters are taken away

parts.note: Casanova was a famous Venetian lover
ca is circa, Latin for about

explanation.surface: A jilted partner weeps as a lover is about to walk out of a dance.
explanation.definitionFit: The bossa nova is a Brazilian dance and musical style related to the samba.

clue.text: Induced judge to imprison rogue after spilling guts

indicators.note: imprisoning someone puts them inside, so one piece sits within another
spilling its guts means losing its insides, so only the outer letters remain

parts.note: 'm'lud' is how a British judge is addressed in court
taken as written

explanation.surface: A judge was persuaded to jail a villain who had confessed everything.
explanation.walkthrough: Spilling one's guts usually means confessing; here the rogue loses its insides instead.
explanation.definitionFit: To lure someone is to entice them, so lured means persuaded or induced.

clue.text: Old cat kept by retiring international US banker

indicators.note: what is kept by something is held inside it
retiring means drawing back, so the word is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: a cap is an international sporting appearance, or the player who wins one
O is the abbreviation for old
a tom is a male cat

explanation.surface: An elderly fat cat looked after by a retired international American banker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Banker' is a crossword favourite for a river, something with banks; the Potomac flows through Washington DC.
explanation.definitionFit: The Potomac is a river in the eastern United States, and a river is a banker in crossword terms.

clue.text: Architect of trendy IOW resort bar last November

parts.note: something trendy is in

indicators.note: bar means except, so the named letter is left out

parts.note: Ventnor is a seaside town on the Isle of Wight
N is November in the NATO alphabet; the last N of the resort goes

explanation.surface: A designer of a fashionable Isle of Wight resort's bar, last seen in November.
explanation.walkthrough: IOW is the Isle of Wight, an island off England's south coast. Its last N removed, the resort becomes VENTOR.
explanation.definitionFit: The architect of a scheme is the person who devised it, which is what an inventor does.

clue.text: Slightly drunk daughters interrupting Thai lady, heartless both

indicators.note: interrupting means breaking into, so one piece is placed inside another
heartless means losing the middle, applied to each of the two words

parts.note: taken as written
D for daughter, twice for the plural
taken as written

explanation.surface: Tipsy daughters butting in on a Thai woman, all of them looking heartless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'both' extends the heartlessness to the Thai as well as the lady.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiddly is informal British for tipsy, mildly drunk.

clue.text: Miss seeing runner compete essentially

parts.note: a ski is a runner that slides over snow

indicators.note: the essence of a word is its heart, so only its central letter is kept

parts.note: the fourth of seven letters is the middle one

explanation.surface: An athlete decides to sit out a race after watching a rival.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Runner' suggests an athlete, but here it is part of a sledge or ski.
explanation.definitionFit: To skip a class or meal is to miss it deliberately, the verb sense of both words.

clue.text: Creature emerging from lake a boar disturbed

indicators.note: disturbed things are thrown out of order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An animal comes out of a lake after a wild pig is startled.
explanation.definitionFit: The koala is an Australian marsupial, an animal and so a creature.

clue.text: Devoutness that is ultimately clear-cut in prebendary's case

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the pieces sit within the outer letters
ultimately means in the end, so the last letter is taken

parts.note: the first and last letters, ignoring the possessive
i.e. abbreviates id est, Latin for that is

indicators.note: the case of a word is its outside, so only its first and last letters are used

parts.note: the final letter

explanation.surface: Holiness that is plainly evident in a cathedral cleric's conduct.
explanation.walkthrough: A prebendary is a senior canon of a cathedral; his 'case' here means the outer letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Piety is religious devotion, so it is the quality of being devout.

clue.text: Dessert prepared to welcome returning sibling

indicators.note: welcoming someone takes them inside, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: set means ready or prepared

indicators.note: returning means coming back, so the word is written the opposite way

parts.note: bro is short for brother

explanation.surface: A pudding made ready for a brother coming home.
explanation.definitionFit: A sorbet is a frozen fruit ice served as a dessert or palate cleanser.

clue.text: Name of couple who disagreed about eating fish

definitions.text: Name of couple who disagreed about eating
definitions.meaning: first meaning: Jack and his wife in the nursery rhyme, who would eat no fat and no lean respectively
second meaning: a small herring-like sea fish

explanation.walkthrough: The nursery rhyme 'Jack Sprat could eat no fat, his wife could eat no lean' gives the couple's surname.
explanation.definitionFit: The surname of the rhyme's couple is also the name of a small oily fish related to the herring.

clue.text: Movie ad, e.g. about Minecraft maybe

indicators.note: turned about suggests letters moved around into a new order

parts.note: the letters of the three words, taken as written

explanation.surface: A film trailer that happens to be about a popular blocky computer game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' reads as 'concerning', but it is the instruction to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Minecraft is a well-known example of the category, hence the 'maybe' marking an example.

clue.text: Incorrect with earlier advanced forecast for corporation

indicators.note: the advanced letter is moved earlier in the word, a small rearrangement of its order

parts.note: something incorrect is bad
an omen forecasts what is to come

explanation.surface: A business tip: a firm's prospects look bad if forecast too early.
explanation.walkthrough: A is the abbreviation for advanced; moving that A to the front of BAD gives ABD. 'Corporation' is an old jocular word for a pot belly.
explanation.definitionFit: Corporation is a humorous dated term for a large belly, and the abdomen is the belly region.

clue.text: Sign right next to unknown public building

parts.note: Libra is a sign of the zodiac
R is the standard abbreviation for right
in algebra x, y and z stand for unknowns

explanation.surface: A sign pointing right beside an anonymous civic building.
explanation.definitionFit: A public library is a civic building housing books for anyone to borrow.

clue.text: Opponent is target for striking female

parts.note: the object of an effort is its target

indicators.note: to strike something out is to cross it off, so a letter is removed

parts.note: taken as written
F is the standard abbreviation for female

explanation.surface: A protester picked out as a target for a woman on strike.
explanation.walkthrough: 'striking female' suggests a stunning woman or one on strike, but the female's abbreviation is struck out.
explanation.definitionFit: An objector is someone who opposes a plan or motion, so an opponent of it.

clue.text: Patient character records broadcast as Mr Average

indicators.note: something broadcast goes out over the airwaves, so it is the sound that counts

parts.note: Job, the Old Testament figure famed for patience, then logs, meaning records

explanation.surface: A doctor's files on a patient go out on air, presented as typical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Patient' looks like a hospital case, but it is the biblical Job, said to rhyme with robe; spoken quickly, 'Job logs' gives the name.
explanation.definitionFit: Joe Bloggs is the British name for a hypothetical ordinary person, the typical man in the street.

clue.text: Committee that possesses enough power to be effective

indicators.note: what a phrase possesses it holds within it, so the letters lie inside these words

parts.note: found across the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A committee that actually has the clout to get things done.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface invites a cryptic definition of a strong committee, but the answer runs across its first two words.
explanation.definitionFit: A law or body said to have teeth has real force, the idiom for effective power.

clue.text: Penning two articles, odd he somehow is impetuous

indicators.note: penning means enclosing as in a pen, so some letters are held inside others
somehow means by some unknown method, so the letters may land in any order

parts.note: taken as written
the definite article the and the indefinite article a

explanation.surface: A strange man, writing two pieces for a paper, is somehow rash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Articles' suggests newspaper pieces, but grammatical articles are meant.
explanation.definitionFit: A hothead acts rashly, so hotheaded means impetuous or quick-tempered.

clue.text: Suspected renegades I'm rushing round to arrest

indicators.note: brought round means turned about, so the letters read backwards
an arrest holds someone captive, so these words hold the letters inside them

parts.note: found across the end of the first word, all of the second and the start of the third

explanation.surface: Turncoats on the run are thought to be facing capture.
explanation.walkthrough: The words look like a chase scene; the answer is concealed backwards across renegaDES I'M RUShing.
explanation.definitionFit: To surmise is to guess without proof, so surmised means suspected or supposed.

clue.text: Victory margin at Ascot perhaps before

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a horse winning by the length of its head
second meaning: in front, in advance

explanation.walkthrough: Ascot is a famous English racecourse; a horse can win by a nose, a neck or a head.
explanation.definitionFit: Winning by a head is a racing margin, while ahead means in front or in advance.

clue.text: Sport mostly needing energy that's excellent

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: diving is an Olympic sport
E is the symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A sport that mainly demands great energy.
explanation.definitionFit: Divine is used informally to mean wonderful or delightful, as in a divine meal.

clue.text: Explosion of temper initially aboard broken-down tour bus

indicators.note: a passenger aboard a vehicle is inside it, so one piece goes within another
something broken down is in pieces, so its letters are reassembled differently

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the neighbouring word

parts.note: the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A tantrum on a coach that has broken down mid-tour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Explosion of temper' looks like the whole definition, but the T of temper is needed in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: An outburst is a sudden explosive release of feeling, like a burst of anger.

clue.text: Shopkeeper's more tough

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a trader who sells meat
second meaning: comparative of butch, meaning rugged or macho

explanation.walkthrough: The 's reads as a possessive but stands for 'is', joining the two meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: A meat retailer runs a shop, and butch means tough-looking, so its comparative means tougher.

clue.text: Good meal must include a posh cake

indicators.note: what must be included is taken inside, so one piece sits within the others

parts.note: G is the abbreviation for good
taken as written
tea is an afternoon or evening meal in Britain
U means upper-class, as opposed to non-U

explanation.surface: A proper meal needs something smart on the menu.
explanation.walkthrough: G, TEA and U are laid end to end, and A goes in after the G.
explanation.definitionFit: A gateau is a rich layered cream cake, from the French word for cake.

clue.text: Country smell, not half like Italian street?

indicators.note: not half means only half survives, so the word loses its second half

parts.note: BO is body odour
taken as written
via is Italian for street

explanation.surface: A wonder whether a country's smell resembles an Italian street.
explanation.walkthrough: BO, short for body odour, is the smell of an unwashed person.
explanation.definitionFit: Bolivia is a landlocked South American country, so it is a straightforward example.

clue.text: Insect husband caught climbing tree

parts.note: a bee is an insect

indicators.note: in a down entry, climbing means reading upwards, so the letters run in reverse

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for husband
C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A husband stung by an insect while climbing a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: The beech is a common deciduous tree with smooth grey bark.

clue.text: Change the name for gas

indicators.note: an instruction to alter, so the following letters must be put in a different order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An instruction to rename a gas, as if rebranding it.
explanation.definitionFit: Methane is a colourless flammable hydrocarbon, the main component of natural gas.

clue.text: Type of male drinkers once outside large pub

indicators.note: outside means surrounding, so these letters wrap around the others

parts.note: Alcoholics Anonymous, whose members are former drinkers
L is the abbreviation for large
PH is the map abbreviation for public house

explanation.surface: A kind of man who used to drink outside a big pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drinkers once' points at reformed drinkers in Alcoholics Anonymous, not drinkers long ago.
explanation.definitionFit: An alpha male is the dominant man in a group, so alpha names a type of male.

clue.text: Designers from Spain sneering, it's out of place

parts.note: E is the international vehicle code for Spain (España)

indicators.note: being out of place means not in the proper order, so letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Spanish designers mocking something that looks out of place.
explanation.definitionFit: Engineers design machines, structures and systems, so they are designers by profession.

clue.text: Rejected oddly empty hotel Democrat publicised

parts.note: H is Hotel in the NATO alphabet

indicators.note: rejected things are sent back, so the letters run the opposite way
oddly points to the letters in odd positions, first, third and fifth

parts.note: the first, third and fifth letters
D is the abbreviation for Democrat

explanation.surface: A spurned Democrat promoted an oddly deserted hotel.
explanation.definitionFit: Something hyped has been heavily promoted or publicised, often beyond its merits.

clue.text: Garden accessory and tools picked up
Flipping embarrassed, a French worker admits secret

indicators.note: to admit is to let in, so one piece is taken inside another

parts.note: un is French for a

indicators.note: flipping something over turns it the other way round

parts.note: embarrassed people go red
a hand is a manual worker, as in farmhand

explanation.surface: A mortified French labourer confesses something he has kept quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flipping' reads as a mild British expletive, but it turns the colour round.
explanation.definitionFit: Underhand dealings are done secretly and deceitfully, so the adjective means sly or covert.
